compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.hw_notes: RTX5090 (Blackwell): high BW HBM-class GDDR7, large L2, abundant SMs, fp16 tensor cores available but problem is small fp16 conv with C_in=16, C_out=32, so MMA is overkill; plain CUDA cores with vectorized fp16 likely sufficient.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.notes: Conv 3x3 with 16->32 channels: 16*32*9 = 4608 MACs per output element times 32*720*1280 outputs (before pool) ~= 1.36e10 MACs. After pool, output is 32x360x640. AvgPool reduces 4 spatial inputs per output. Arithmetic intensity moderate; mostly memory-bound for activations.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.risk: fp16 accumulation precision; need fp32 accumulate

memory_bandwidth.notes: Input: 1*16*720*1280*2B = ~29.5 MB. Weights: 32*16*9*2B = 9 KB (fits in shared/registers easily). Output: 32*360*640*2B = ~14.7 MB. Fusing conv+relu+avgpool avoids writing intermediate ~58 MB conv output to global mem -- major win.
memory_bandwidth.risk: Halo / boundary handling for 3x3 conv with padding=1; multiple reads of input rows.

register_pressure.notes: If each thread computes a 2x2 output block (one pooled output = 2x2 conv outputs), it needs 32 fp32 accumulators across out channels per pooled point -> too many. Better: each block/warp produces tile of pooled outputs for subset of out channels.
register_pressure.risk: Splitting C_out across blocks reduces fusion benefit only marginally because input is reread per group.

nodes.notes: 1) Classification: dense stencil (3x3 conv) + elementwise (ReLU) + pooling reduction (2x2 avg). All fusable. 2) Math: y[oc,oh,ow] = avg_{i,j in 2x2}( relu( sum_{ic,kh,kw} x[ic, 2oh+i+kh-1, 2ow+j+kw-1]*W[oc,ic,kh,kw] + b[oc] ) ). Output shape: 1x32x360x640 fp16. 3) Layout: NCHW fp16 contiguous; input 1x16x720x1280, weights 32x16x3x3 small, fits in shared/constant. 4) Regimes: (a) memory-bound activation streaming - dominant; (b) compute-bound if poor reuse; (c) latency-bound if too few blocks. 5) Knobs: tile size (output tile in pooled space), C_out blocking, vectorization (half2/float4), shared mem for input halo tile, register accumulators, fp32 accumulate. 6) Skeleton: each block handles tile of pooled outputs (e.g., 16x16 pooled = 32x32 conv outputs needing 34x34 halo) for ALL 32 out channels; load input halo per ic into shared, accumulate into 32 fp32 register accums per thread-output; ReLU; 2x2 average; write fp16 out. 7) Families: (F1) FULL FUSION single kernel: shared-mem tile + register accumulators over all 32 oc — TOP CHOICE since weights (9KB) fit. (F2) Two-stage conv-fused-relu then pool — wastes BW. (F3) im2col+GEMM — overkill for 16->32. SELF_CHECK: F1 chosen. Working set fits: weights 4608 fp16=9KB constant; halo tile e.g., 16ic*34*34*2B = ~37KB shared (feasible per SM).

action.description: Single fused CUDA kernel: each block produces a tile of pooled outputs (e.g., 16x16 pooled = 32x32 conv outputs) for all 32 output channels. Load input halo tile (16 in-channels, 34x34) into shared memory in stages; each thread holds per-oc fp32 accumulators for its 2x2 conv-output sub-tile, applies ReLU, averages over 2x2 to produce one pooled fp16 output per oc. Weights stored in constant or shared memory. Uses fp32 accumulation, fp16 I/O.
action.rationale: Avoids writing the 58MB conv intermediate to global memory; reuses halo via shared memory across 3x3 stencil; weights tiny and reused fully.
action.title: Full-fusion tiled kernel (conv+ReLU+avgpool) with shared-mem halo

compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.hw_notes: RTX5090 ample shared memory per SM (>100KB); fp16 vector loads (half2) align well with C_in=16.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.notes: Reuses 4x4 patch for 4 pooled outputs; weights in constant memory; good FMA density.

memory_bandwidth.notes: Conv intermediate kept in registers; only input read and pooled output written.

register_pressure.notes: 32 OC * 4 floats per thread = 128 regs/thread of accumulators; launch_bounds(128,4) constrains occupancy.

nodes.notes: CURRENT: does= single fused kernel computes 2x2 pooled tile over all 32 OC by reading 16 IC halo tiles into smem (double-buffered) and accumulating 4 conv outputs per thread in registers, then bias+ReLU+avgpool. bottleneck= compute/register pressure (high reg usage limits occupancy; fp32 math on fp16 data). FOLLOW_THROUGH: aligned_with_intent=yes. UPDATE_BELIEF: 6.68x speedup confirms the fusion + smem-halo approach is excellent; next bet= push toward tensor-core mma (HMMA) or warp-level cooperative reduction to exploit fp16 compute, and/or reduce register pressure by blocking OC.

action.description: Each block produces a pooled output tile for a SUBSET of output channels (e.g., 8 or 16 oc per block). Reduces register pressure and allows higher thread occupancy. Input halo is loaded once per block and reused across the oc subset.
action.rationale: Trades a small amount of input re-read (halo loaded for multiple oc-groups) for much better register pressure and occupancy.

action.description: Fused kernel where each thread directly produces ONE pooled output (one (oh_p, ow_p, oc) point) by reading the 4x4 conv-input footprint (2x2 pooled stride x 3x3 kernel with overlap = effective 4x4 input window) without using shared memory — relying instead on L1/L2 cache for halo reuse across neighboring threads. Weights placed in constant memory.
action.rationale: Simplest implementation; small C_in=16 means each thread does 16*9*4=576 FMAs (or 16*16 with shared 2x2 conv outputs reuse). Useful as a baseline and possibly competitive due to good L1/L2 cache behavior on RTX5090.

kernel_summary: Fuse Conv2d(3x3, pad=1, stride=1) + ReLU + AvgPool2d(2x2) on fp16 NCHW input 1x16x720x1280 producing fp16 1x32x360x640. Weights are tiny (32x16x3x3 = 9KB fp16) and fully cacheable in constant/shared memory. The reference's main waste is the 58MB intermediate conv output written to global memory; full fusion into one kernel removes that traffic, making the problem activation-bandwidth bound. Key constraints: fp16 input/output with fp32 accumulation for accuracy (rtol=atol=0.01), padding=1 boundary handling, halo overlap of 3x3 stencil with 2x2 pooling (each pooled output depends on a 4x4 input window per in-channel after combining stride-1 conv + stride-2 pool). RTX5090 (Blackwell) offers plentiful shared memory, large L2, and high BW which favors a tiled fused kernel.
